Kiddushin 39b_8-10.notes: This is a tricky case but it is actually part of the Gemara's commentary on the story. In this commentary the gemara revises some of the story, or adds some details. But these are of the Gemara's efforts to resolve certain issues. So I would not include them in the story at all, although, at some level, they influence the audience's understanding of the story.

Gittin 57b_0-4.notes: This is a full blown story, but it is about biblical characters, not rabbis. So it is not in the class of stories that we are looking at. (I put the confidence is right, that it is a story. But not our kind of story.)

Gittin 68a_7-12.quote_start: As it is written with regard to the building of the Temple: “For the house, when it was being built, was built of stone made ready at the quarry
Gittin 68a_7-12.notes: Again, this is a full story but about biblical characters. So not in our scope, which is rabbis and post-biblical figures.

Ketubot 7a_1-1.notes: This is borderline. It is mostly speech acts: A rabbi permits a groom to have sex on Shabbat, the rabbis respond, and he responds back. So technically there is not enough actions. But there is conflict and some implied change, so it is borderline.

Ketubot 112a_11-11.notes: Again, mainly a dialogue, so lacking the actions necessary for a story. But has conflict, so can be borderline.

Ketubot 15a_0-0.notes: This is just not enough to go on to be counted as a story or even a narrative. It is a legal discussion discussing facts of an incident and their consequences, but not enough of the incident is given.

Yevamot 15a_14-14.quote_start: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁלִּיקֵּט אֶתְרוֹג בְּאֶחָד בִּשְׁבָט, וְנָהַג בּוֹ שְׁנֵי עִשּׂוּרִין.
Yevamot 15a_14-14.quote_end: אֶחָד כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וְאֶחָד כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
Yevamot 15a_14-14.notes: This part that is highlighted is the gemara's comment about the story. It does tell you about what R. Akiva was thinking, but it is not part of the story. There is no real story here, just a report of what R. Akiva did in the preceding lines. I have indicated where that report begins and ends for the boundaries. But it is not really a story.

Yevamot 17a_4-4.notes: This is not a story. There is a description of rabbi's sitting in a certain arrangement. But then they just have a discussion about some distant future events.

Yevamot 105a_13-13.quote_start: רַבָּה וְאַבָּיֵי מִדְּבֵית עֵלִי קָאָתוּרַבָּה וְאַבָּיֵי מִדְּבֵית עֵלִי קָאָתוּ,
Yevamot 105a_13-13.quote_end: אַבָּיֵי דַּעֲסַק בְּתוֹרָה וּבִגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים — חֲיָה שִׁיתִּין שְׁנִין.

Yevamot 106b_9-9.notes: This is just a description of what Mar Zutra did--how he prepared a document.   But the objection is not necessarily against him. It is a general objection to his practice. (and even if it were against him, the narrative ends there. There is no continuation.)   And then you have the gemara making a legal ruling, which is not part of the narrative at all. So there is no story here.
